1.

This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act of 1988') has been Smt. Kunti Jharna vs Jaswant Singh on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118876792/
1 filed by the claimants / appellants aggrieved by award dated 21/09/2016 passed in claim case No.132/2015 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bemetara, District - Bemetara (CG).
2. Facts of the case in brief is that the claimants/appellants filed an application under Section 166 read with Section 140 of the Act of 1988 claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.28,67,832/- on account of death of the deceased - Ruben Joseph in an accident which took place on 10/11/2012 at about 8 PM when he was coming home on his motor cycle to Dantewada from Jagdalpur due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (truck) bearing No.CG 17 SS 1250.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are the mother and sister of the deceased.

Learned Tribunal, after appreciating the evidence on record,
granted compensation to the tune of Rs.3,13,000/- in favour of the claimants.
3. The claim application was resisted by respondents 1 and 2 and filed their written statement.

They pleaded that the deceased was rashly and negligently riding the motor cycle and while overtaking his friends who were on the other motor cycle, he collided with the back side of the truck and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the truck.
4. Respondent No.3 / insurance company also denied the averments of the claim application.
It has been pleaded that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle and the deceased had no valid and effective driving license.

Therefore, in the absence of valid driving license,
the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.
5. Learned Tribunal framed as many as 7 issues.
The issue with regard to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1 / driver thereby causing death of Ruben Joseph has been decided in favour of the claimants.
2nd issue with regard to negligent riding of the motor cycle of the deceased was not found proved.
3rd issue with regard to driver of the truck not having valid and driving license has not been found proved.
4 th issue with regard to Rs.16000/- as income of the deceased was also not found proved.
5th issue with regard to entitlement of compensation has been partially proved.
6th issue with regard to relief and cost has been accepted.
7th issue with regard to entitlement of compensation of respondent No.2 and respondent No.4 has been found proved.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants argued that the learned Tribunal wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- despite evidence produced before it that the deceased was working as sub-dealer of Sonalika Tractor and was also working as Journalist in a local news paper and used to earn Rs.16,000/- per month, which is absolutely perverse and liable to be set aside.

He further submits that the learned Tribunal ought to have granted future prospects to the claimants /
appellants.
He further submits that the compensation awarded on other conventional heads are also on the lower side which requires suitable enhancement.

7. Learned counsel for respondent No3/ Insurance Company supported the award passed by the learned Tribunal and submitted that it is evident that the deceased was not holding any driving license, therefore, the compensation awarded is just and proper.
He prays that the appeal may be dismissed.

Smt. Kunti Jharna vs Jaswant Singh on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118876792/
2
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and also perused the records.
9. The date of incident is 10/11/2012.
The learned Tribunal on the basis of evidence on record disbelieved the income of the deceased.
This finding does not appear to be perverse, hence affirmed.
Learned Tribunal has considered the monthly income of the deceased as Rs3000/-.
Monthly income assessed by learned Tribunal is on the lower side and needs suitable enhancement.

Looking to the evidence available on record, prevailing minimum wages and aged of the deceased, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the monthly income ought to have been considered as Rs.4,500/-.
Looking to the age, 40% future prospects ought to have been added.

Therefore, it would be appropriate to modify the assessment of compensation in the light of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009) 6 SCC 121,
National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and ors, (2018) 18 SCC 130.

10. Rest of the conditions of the impugned award is not disturbed.
The learned Tribunal will apportion the enhanced amount of compensation as per terms of award.
11. No order as to cost.
